postcards.title: Rain Gauge Railway Detail Ticket
postcards.useCase: Printable postcard for a child who wants to thank someone for a gift, favor, visit, lesson, or shared activity without mentioning price or private details.
postcards.adultSetup: Print one postcard, set out a pencil, and ask the writer to choose one small true detail they appreciated before inventing the railway part.
postcards.kidDirection: Write a sincere thank-you sentence, then turn the appreciated detail into a tiny Rain Gauge Railway ticket clue.
postcards.noteStarter: Thank you for __________; one detail I noticed and appreciated was __________.
postcards.storyBridge: In Rain Gauge Railway, that kind thing becomes a station ticket marked with __________.
postcards.politeClose: My polite closing sentence will say __________.
postcards.drawingPrompt: Draw a rain gauge, a train ticket, and the ordinary object I appreciated: __________.
postcards.revisionNudge: Check that the note names one specific detail instead of only saying nice; my detail is __________.
postcards.quietOption: If I want a quiet start, I can point to the detail card and write __________.
postcards.takeHomeLine: A sincere thank-you note can remember one small detail like __________.

postcards.title: Seed Library Kind Sentence Card
postcards.useCase: Printable postcard for homeschool, tutoring, or family table practice when the child needs help writing one warm sentence of thanks.
postcards.adultSetup: Print one card and invite the writer to pick a pretend seed packet, map mark, or drawer label that can carry a kind sentence.
postcards.kidDirection: Write one clear kind sentence, then let the Seed Library Map Room turn it into a catalog note.
postcards.noteStarter: Thank you for __________; it helped me feel __________.
postcards.storyBridge: In Seed Library Map Room, the thank-you sentence is filed in a drawer labeled __________.
postcards.politeClose: The kind closing words I want to use are __________.
postcards.drawingPrompt: Draw a seed packet, a map corner, and one helpful object from the thank-you: __________.
postcards.revisionNudge: Reread the sentence and make sure it sounds kind and clear by adding __________.
postcards.quietOption: If I want to work silently, I can choose a seed packet word and write __________.
postcards.takeHomeLine: A kind thank-you sentence can make the reader remember __________.

postcards.title: Greenhouse Gear Gift Bridge Postcard
postcards.useCase: Printable postcard for turning a gift, borrowed object, useful supply, or helpful gesture into a tiny invented garden detail.
postcards.adultSetup: Print one postcard and remind the writer to describe how the gift or kindness was useful without writing about cost.
postcards.kidDirection: Name what you are thankful for, then imagine it as a gentle greenhouse gear that helps a pretend garden scene.
postcards.noteStarter: Thank you for __________; I used it or remembered it when __________.
postcards.storyBridge: In Greenhouse Gear Garden, the thank-you gift turns into a garden gear that helps __________.
postcards.politeClose: A polite ending I can add is __________.
postcards.drawingPrompt: Draw the greenhouse gear beside the real-life thing I am thankful for: __________.
postcards.revisionNudge: Make the bridge clearer by adding how the gift or kindness helped: __________.
postcards.quietOption: If I am not ready to talk, I can sketch the gear first and label it __________.
postcards.takeHomeLine: A gift-to-story bridge connects real thanks to one invented detail: __________.

postcards.title: Pantry Measurement Memory Note
postcards.useCase: Printable postcard for a child writing thanks after a meal, class activity, errand help, visit, or ordinary shared moment.
postcards.adultSetup: Print the postcard and help the writer choose one simple memory detail such as a color, sound, tool, snack, book, or table object.
postcards.kidDirection: Write one thank-you memory detail, then make it part of a cozy pantry measurement clue.
postcards.noteStarter: Thank you for __________; I remember when __________.
postcards.storyBridge: In Pantry Measurement Mystery, that memory becomes a measuring-cup clue beside __________.
postcards.politeClose: My closing line of thanks will be __________.
postcards.drawingPrompt: Draw a measuring spoon trail and the memory detail I want to keep: __________.
postcards.revisionNudge: Add one exact memory word so the reader can picture __________.
postcards.quietOption: If I want a quiet version, I can list three memory words first: __________.
postcards.takeHomeLine: A thank-you note feels more sincere when it includes a remembered detail like __________.

postcards.title: Tidepool Timekeepers Polished Thanks
postcards.useCase: Printable postcard for revising a first thank-you draft so it sounds complete, warm, and easy to read.
postcards.adultSetup: Print one postcard and invite the writer to draft first, then revise one word, one detail, and one closing line without any score or speed goal.
postcards.kidDirection: Write a first thank-you line, add a Tidepool Timekeepers lab detail, and polish one sentence so it sounds finished.
postcards.noteStarter: Thank you for __________; my first draft says __________.
postcards.storyBridge: In Tidepool Timekeepers Lab, the polished sentence glows inside a minute jar labeled __________.
postcards.politeClose: After revision, my polite close will read __________.
postcards.drawingPrompt: Draw a tidepool clock, a minute jar, and one polished thank-you word: __________.
postcards.revisionNudge: Polish the note by replacing one plain word with __________.
postcards.quietOption: If I want to revise quietly, I can underline one sentence and improve __________.
postcards.takeHomeLine: A polished thank-you postcard keeps the same thanks but makes one part clearer: __________.
